prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Miami. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Miami for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — but first a quick question: do you want practices near a specific Miami neighborhood or ZIP code (e.g., Brickell, Coral Gables, Miami Beach, Doral)? Also tell me whether this is a single-tooth implant, multiple implants/full-arch, whether you have a timeline, and if insurance/price is important. If you give that, I’ll prepare a targeted list of specific offices to call and explain why each is a good fit.

In the meantime, here’s practical, immediately useful guidance so you can start calling today.

Which types of practices to call (and why)
- Oral & maxillofacial surgeons (OMS): best for complex surgical cases (bone grafts, sinus lifts, impacted teeth, sedation/general anesthesia). They place implants surgically and manage surgical risks.
- Periodontists: specialists in gums and supporting bone; excellent for implants when there is periodontal disease or need for grafting.
- Prosthodontists: specialists in complex restorative work and full-mouth reconstructions; call them if you want the best cosmetic and functional tooth restorations (crowns/bridges/overdentures).
- Multidisciplinary implant centers: often have surgeons + prosthodontists + CBCT and digital labs in one place — convenient and good for coordinated care.
- General dentists with advanced implant training: fine for straightforward single-tooth implants or when you prefer continuity of your general dentist restoring the crown. Confirm their implant experience.

What to ask when you call (phone script / checklist)
Use this short script and checklist so you can compare offices consistently:
- “Do you place dental implants in-house, and who places them (OMS, periodontist, prosthodontist, general dentist)?”
- “How many implants does the provider place per year? What is their experience with cases like mine (single vs full-arch, bone grafts, sinus lifts)?”
- “Do you use a CBCT (3D) scan for planning? Do you offer guided implant surgery or same-day temporary teeth?”
- “Who will do the final restoration (crown/bridge/prosthesis)? Is that person an in‑office specialist or an outside lab?”
- “What implant systems do you use (Straumann, Nobel Biocare, Zimmer, etc.) and what warranty or follow-up care do you provide?”
- “Do you offer sedation (IV, oral) if I’m anxious? What are sedation costs and requirements?”
- “Estimated cost range for my case (single implant w/ crown vs bone graft vs full-arch)? Do you accept my insurance? Any financing or payment plans?”
- “Can I see before/after photos and patient references or reviews? Can I get a written treatment plan and breakdown of fees after the consultation?”

Red flags to avoid
- No CBCT when a 3D scan is needed (complex cases, bone loss, sinus proximity).
- No clear plan for who restores the implant (surgery done by one provider but crown/bridge left ambiguous).
- Pressure to choose the cheapest system without explanation.
- No written estimate or unwillingness to explain alternatives.
- Poor or no credential transparency (who performs surgery, their specialty).

How to compare quotes
- Make sure each quote includes: CBCT, surgical placement, implant fixture brand, abutment, temporary tooth (if needed), final restoration cost, grafts (if needed), and follow-up visits.
- Don’t compare only total price — compare what’s included and the experience level of the provider.

If you tell me your ZIP or neighborhood and your case type, I’ll prepare a curated list of 5–7 specific Miami practices to call, with short reasons why each might be a good fit (specialty, services, technology, and what to ask them).
